To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
End users need visual interfaces to compose data sources, but the interfaces need to be flexible enough to support a wide range of users and tasks."

1) the user should be able to compose a query in a natural way; 2) the query should be executed in the background; 3) the user should get a preview of the results; 4) the user should see how to refine the results.

1) the most important requirement for end users when accessing data sources is the ability to visualize the content, 2) the ability to visualize content is a necessary but not sufficient requirement for end users to compose data sources, and 3) the ability to compose data sources is necessary to enable end users to create their own applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of paradigms for the visual composition of data sources.
the definition of paradigms for data source exploration, composition and visualization, which are accessible to non technical users.
the development of tools that allow end users to access and integrate data sources in a visual way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study showed that the end users are interested in accessing data sources and composing them, but they need to be supported by tools that make this task easier.
end users need to be supported by a system that provides a visual composition of data sources.
end users are not interested in the technical details of data sources, they just want to be able to compose data sources to create their own personalized data sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for visual data source composition and we have implemented a prototype for this approach.
we are able to provide a visual environment for laypeople to explore and compose Web Services.
we have defined a set of mechanisms to enable laypeople to explore, compose and integrate data sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
end users have a strong desire to be able to access and compose data sources, and that they can express requirements that go beyond the current state of the art in this field.

laypeople are not only interested in composing data sources, but they also want to explore them in an intuitive manner, in order to understand the structure of their content and the way it can be exploited.
end users can be involved in the design of data integration systems, which are then able to provide them with a user-friendly interface for exploring and integrating data sources.
